CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST ANSWER, and it is the round's best lesson: I measured `q.stages` at 0/94 shipped quests and cut it as a dead read of the r.frame kind. WRONG. tools/lib/gamedata.mjs loadQuests() admits TWO document shapes — `doc.quests[]` and a bare `doc.stages && doc.id`. A stage-shaped quest (quests/the-boards.json) landed mid-run and my cut turned it into 495 signatures FAILing 'quest declares no resolutions' — a tool defect published as a build defect. A field census over shipped DATA cannot establish that a read is dead; the LOADER defines what shapes are legal and the data catches up later. Fixed: stage-shaped quests are UNMEASURABLE ('no predicate in this tool'), with the file's own declared_incomplete carried through.

A fallback onto a field the engine ignores would resolve a giver the running build leaves unresolved — a permissive substitution of exactly the kind defect B was. Removed.

notes_for_successor: Design decision: keep the walk player-optimal (viability = does ANY route exist) but every grant must be DERIVED from shipped data. Where a token is granted without a producing source in data, evaluate the quest twice (full grant vs provable-only grant); if the verdicts differ the criterion is `unmeasurable` and the token is named. That makes a permissive substitution structurally unable to produce a silent pass.
